solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Vote against holding old runner in battle site

indicators.note: holding says the word for voting against grips the runner's name between its letters

parts.note: nay is a vote against
Seb Coe, the former Olympic middle-distance runner

explanation.surface: Somebody opposes keeping a retired athlete at a historic battlefield.
explanation.walkthrough: SEB is Seb Coe, a British Olympic champion of the 1980s. NASEBY was a decisive battle of the English Civil War, in Northamptonshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Naseby in Northamptonshire was where Cromwell's New Model Army routed the Royalists in 1645.

clue.text: Get annoyed dropping a couple of grand in river

indicators.note: in says the two letters are dropped into the river's name

parts.note: the Nile is the great African river
G is slang for a grand, a thousand, so two of them give GG

explanation.surface: Someone loses their temper after letting two thousand pounds fall into a river.
explanation.definitionFit: To niggle is to irritate in a petty way, or to be bothered by small things.

clue.text: South African sportsman brings Kop frenzy

indicators.note: frenzy suggests wild disorder, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A South African player whips the Liverpool fans into a frenzy.
explanation.walkthrough: The Kop is the famous terrace at Liverpool's Anfield ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Springboks is the nickname of South Africa's national rugby team, so one of its players is a springbok.

clue.text: Cover that's seen through England batsman's clash

parts.note: Ian Bell batted for England in Test cricket
to jar is to clash or conflict

explanation.surface: A transparent cover protects an England cricketer from a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A bell jar is a bell-shaped glass cover, transparent so its contents can be seen.

clue.text: TV quiz to encourage top teachers

parts.note: to egg on is to encourage
heads are head teachers, the top staff in a school

explanation.surface: A television quiz show is urged to recruit leading schoolteachers.
explanation.walkthrough: EGGHEADS is a long-running BBC quiz in which teams take on a panel of quiz champions.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggheads is the title of a British television quiz show.

clue.text: Sort of paper treated opera-goers fine

indicators.note: treated suggests something processed and altered, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Audience members at the opera are given special treatment and charged a penalty.
explanation.definitionFit: Greaseproof paper is a kitchen paper that resists oil and fat.

clue.text: Wild rush led athletics event

indicators.note: wild suggests disorder, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A frantic charge set off a race on the track.
explanation.definitionFit: The hurdles is a race in which athletes jump a series of barriers.

clue.text: Like to confine a shaky tree

parts.note: as means like, in the same way as
to pen animals is to confine them

explanation.surface: Someone wants to fence in a wobbly tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The aspen is a poplar whose leaves quiver in the slightest breeze, often called the trembling poplar.

clue.text: Prepares tomatoes for Italian restaurant's various items

definitions.meaning: split into two words, it describes drying tomatoes under the sun

explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, the answer describes how sun-dried tomatoes are made.
explanation.definitionFit: Sundries are miscellaneous small items not worth listing separately.

clue.text: Make a mess of role initially taken by old film star

indicators.note: taken by says the letter is received inside the star's surname

parts.note: Clark Gable, Hollywood star of Gone with the Wind

indicators.note: initially picks out the first letter of the word role

explanation.surface: An ageing movie star bungles a part from the start.
explanation.definitionFit: To garble a message is to jumble it so it comes out muddled.

clue.text: One slow to move making mistake in simple goal

indicators.note: in puts the word for mistake inside the easy goal

parts.note: a tap-in is a very easy goal scored from close range
to err is to make a mistake

explanation.surface: A footballer fluffs an easy chance at goal and is called a slowcoach.
explanation.walkthrough: ERR is a verb, but crosswords freely use it for a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrapin is a freshwater turtle, a slow-moving reptile.

clue.text: Character created by Robert Louis S pants

parts.note: Long John Silver is the pirate created by Robert Louis Stevenson in Treasure Island
the bare initial standing for Stevenson's surname, used as written

explanation.surface: A Stevenson character sounds as if he is in his underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue shortens Stevenson to S, so the character's name comes from 'Robert Louis' and the S is added on. In British English 'pants' are underpants.
explanation.definitionFit: Long johns are warm underwear with full-length legs, and pants in Britain means underwear.

clue.text: Cheating outlaw with family in flight

parts.note: Robin Hood is the legendary outlaw

indicators.note: in says the family word goes inside the word for flight

parts.note: wing as in taking wing, flight
kin are one's family

explanation.surface: An outlaw and his relatives are cheating while on the run.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoodwinking means deceiving or tricking someone.

clue.text: Vessel ultimately represented by 'Queen Elizabeth'

indicators.note: ultimately takes only the final letter of the word vessel

parts.note: something represented by a person or thing is in it, so this gives IN
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the royal cipher of Queen Elizabeth

explanation.surface: A ship is portrayed in the end by the famous Cunard name.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: the Queen Elizabeth was a famous ocean passenger ship.
explanation.definitionFit: The Queen Elizabeth was a great Cunard ocean passenger ship, the classic example of this type of vessel.

clue.text: Girl in lobby, one making flying visit

parts.note: bird is British slang for a girl or young woman
in can mean of, as in 'the best in the land'
a passage or entrance hall can be a lobby

explanation.surface: A young woman waiting in a hallway is only dropping by briefly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Girl in lobby' looks like a container, but the pieces simply run in order, with 'in' giving OF.
explanation.definitionFit: A migrating bird passes through briefly, so the phrase describes a person who never stays long anywhere.

clue.text: Consuming Old Peculiar see a lush in such places?

indicators.note: consuming means taking in, so the reworked letters swallow the single letter
peculiar means odd, so the letters are put in a strange order

explanation.surface: Watch a drunk knocking back a strong ale in the pubs he frequents.
explanation.walkthrough: Old Peculier is a famous strong English ale, which the surface plays on. 'Consuming' puts O inside ALEHUSES (the anagram of SEE A LUSH, from 'Peculiar').
explanation.definitionFit: Alehouses are pubs, exactly the sort of places where a drunk drinks beer.

clue.text: Some debs settled in relief

indicators.note: settled suggests being placed into a new arrangement, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Several debutantes calmed down with a sigh of relief.
explanation.walkthrough: Debs are debutantes, young society women. 'in relief' is the sculptural sense, raised from a surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Embossed designs are raised from the surface, which is what carved or moulded in relief means.

clue.text: Sulk about a top man who gets English having fun

indicators.note: about says the word for sulk goes round the other pieces

parts.note: to mope is to sulk gloomily
a king is the top man in a kingdom

explanation.surface: A monarch who is sulking cheers up once an Englishman joins him.
explanation.definitionFit: Making whoopee is an informal idiom for boisterous merrymaking, revelry or lovemaking.

clue.text: Some fantasise mentally overturning unbeatable opponent

indicators.note: overturning in a down clue means the letters are read upwards, from end to start
some says only part of the words fantasise mentally is taken

explanation.surface: A person dreams in their head of turning over an invincible foe.
explanation.walkthrough: The run SISEMEN, read backwards, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A nemesis is an arch-enemy or opponent one can never defeat.

clue.text: Warn of drink leading to death

parts.note: port is a fortified wine
one's end is one's death

explanation.surface: A warning that alcohol will be the death of someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To portend is to foreshadow, give warning of something to come.

clue.text: Like seabird on back of ship

parts.note: as means like
the tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: Like a gull perched at the stern of a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Astern means at or towards the rear of a ship.

clue.text: What prisoners picked tree with little hesitation

parts.note: the oak is a common tree
um is a short sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Convicts were made to choose a tree after a brief pause.
explanation.walkthrough: Picking oakum, teasing old tarred rope into loose fibres, was a traditional task given to Victorian prisoners and workhouse inmates.
explanation.definitionFit: Oakum was the loose fibre that prisoners unpicked from old ropes, used to caulk ships' seams.

clue.text: Rogue mentioned in middle of church

indicators.note: mentioned says the words are spoken, so what counts is how they sound

parts.note: the nave is the central body of a church

explanation.surface: A scoundrel is talked about in the centre of the church.
explanation.definitionFit: A knave is a dishonest man, a rogue or scoundrel.

clue.text: Wicked intelligence about a fire raging

indicators.note: about says the word for intelligence goes round the reshuffled letters

parts.note: nous is common sense or intelligence

indicators.note: raging suggests wild turmoil, so the letters of a fire are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone with evil cunning starts a blaze that burns out of control.
explanation.definitionFit: Nefarious is a synonym of wicked or villainous.

clue.text: Fur encloses relation

parts.note: to seal something is to close it up completely
kin are one's relatives

explanation.surface: A fur coat is wrapped around a family member.
explanation.definitionFit: Sealskin is the fur of the seal, once prized for coats.

clue.text: Person who's let the French understand

parts.note: les is the French plural form of 'the'
to see is to understand

explanation.surface: Someone who has been permitted grasps the French language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Person who's let' means a person who is let a property, not one who lets it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenant holding a lease is someone to whom a property has been let.

clue.text: Doctor replacing first item of communication mounted competition

indicators.note: replacing the first item of says the opening letter of the message word is swapped out

parts.note: a message is a communication

explanation.surface: A physician substitutes for the first item on the agenda at a meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mounted' means on horseback, not set up.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressage is an equestrian event judged on the precision of a horse's trained movements, a competition on horseback.

clue.text: Strange child most likely to come up

parts.note: odd means strange
a son is a child

explanation.surface: A peculiar boy is tipped to arrive soon.
explanation.definitionFit: In betting, an odds-on chance is the favourite, more likely than not to happen.
